reason: A proxy that checks keys, enforces caps, routes big orders to a person and has a kill switch is a quarter's work for my team, and we'd own it instead of putting a startup's code in front of customer order flow. The price isn't the problem; we just build this kind of thing ourselves.
objection: A vendor with no customers and no SOC 2 sitting in our order path, even in shadow mode. Vendor risk review and security sign-off would cost more staff time than the $1,500, and if they fold in two years I'm left with a control I can't maintain in front of FINRA.
would_change_my_mind: My engineering lead telling me we can't ship the equivalent, exam-ready control mapping included, inside a quarter.
